comments.author: Guilder
comments.body:
Just as a heads-up, I discovered (thanks to a list of World Clock recipes) that Amsterdam currently hosts not one, but two Southeast/East Asian themed recipe books. They can be found with the following NPCs:

Fabric Dealer (outside of Merchant Guild):
Sew Javanese Batik (r9 sewing)
Sew Chinese Calico (r12 sewing)
Sew Okinawan Bingata (r12 sewing)
Sew Chinese Rugs (r13 sewing)
Sew Japanese Brocade (r13 sewing)

Tailor (seated at the back of the Tavern)
....Too many recipes to list reasonably. Here's a partial list of what you can make (with pictures):

eririndol.blog.fc2.com/blog-entry-114.html

Additionally, there are quite a few other recipes floating in and around Europe. Some have been reported on the DB before now, while some haven't. For your viewing pleasure:

lisdol.blog.fc2.com/blog-entry-208.html

Have fun, then. And sorry for posting all the info under here -- couldn't think of a better place to put it.

comments.author: SeaRaven
comments.body: Does anyone else have to make a new account everytime they log on here? I wrote passwords and account names down after the first few times its said that I was giving the wrong information. Still it says the information I'm giving is wrong. So I make a new account everytime I want to log in and comment. Anyone have some tips or insight?

comments.author: Curious
comments.body: I've never had a problem logging in.

comments.author: V_I
comments.body: Well, I did have one problem with account making here. Basically, I had too long of an account name when I registered, and half of the letters got lopped off once registration was finished. So my account name went from being like ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP to being ABCDEF. I could still log into that account with my password, but only by removing the letters which no longer 'existed'. Your problem may be that, or it could be something else entirely.

comments.author: WW
comments.body:
It could also be your password creation. Sometimes you are allowed to use special characters like !@#$% etc in your password when registering an account, but can't actually use those characters when you try to loggin.

I don't know if Ivyro has that problem, but you might want to try it out.
